A_target.statement:
Let $A \subseteq X$ be [[Definition:Topological Space|topological spaces]].
Then the [[Definition:Relative Homology|relative homology]] of the pair is:
:$\map {H_n} {X, A} = \map {H_n} {\map {C_\bullet} X / \map {C_\bullet} A}$

B_source.statement:
Let $D_\bullet$ be a [[Definition:Subcomplex|subcomplex]] of a [[Definition:Chain Complex|chain complex]] $C_\bullet$.
Then $C_\bullet / D_\bullet$ is a chain complex with the induced differential.

substitutions.the ambient chain complex: the singular chains of the larger space
substitutions.the subcomplex collapsed: the singular chains supported in the subspace
substitutions.the quotient complex: the relative chain complex of the pair

derived.the induced differential on the quotient: relative cycles are chains whose boundary lies in the subspace
derived.the homology of the quotient complex: the relative homology groups of the pair

validity_conditions: The chains of the subspace form a subcomplex, since the boundary of a chain supported in the subspace is again supported there.
The differential therefore descends to the quotient, and a relative cycle is a chain whose boundary lies in the subspace rather than vanishing.
The resulting long exact sequence of the pair comes from the short exact sequence of complexes, which is available precisely because the construction is a quotient by a subcomplex.
proof_plan: Take the [[Definition:Singular Chain|singular chains]] $\map {C_\bullet} X$ and the chains $\map {C_\bullet} A$ of simplices lying in $A$.

The boundary of a simplex in $A$ lies in $A$, so $\map \partial {\map {C_n} A} \subseteq \map {C_{n - 1} } A$.
Hence $\map {C_\bullet} A$ is a [[Definition:Subcomplex|subcomplex]].

By the source result, $\map {C_\bullet} X / \map {C_\bullet} A$ is a chain complex with:
:$\map {\bar \partial} {c + \map {C_n} A} = \partial c + \map {C_{n - 1} } A$

Define $\map {H_n} {X, A}$ as the homology of this quotient complex.
{{qed}}
